page: Google Cloud Platform n4-highmem-16 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the n4 server family. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical Intel cores with hyperthreading enabled, providing 2 threads per core. The instance is equipped with 128.0 GB of RAM, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. The CPU cache configuration includes 48 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a large 260 MB L3 cache. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and has zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results place the n4-highmem-16 in the average performance tier across most metrics. The single-core stress-ng CPU performance is measured at 1563.58, while multi-core performance reaches 12846.34. Memory bandwidth tests show 1084.69 GB/sec for cached small-block reads, dropping to 115.64 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 66.19 GB/sec for uncached large-block writes. Notably, the server demonstrates strong performance in Geekbench text processing with a score of 2375.0, while its overall Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores are 1836.0 and 10971.0, respectively.

The Intel processor supports advanced instruction sets, including Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX_TILE, AMX_INT8) and Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512), which facilitate vector and matrix operations. In LLM inference benchmarks using a small 135M model, the server achieves a prompt processing speed of 1277.73 tokens/sec and a text generation speed of 262.3 tokens/sec. For a medium 7B model, prompt processing drops to 90.56 tokens/sec and text generation to 11.28 tokens/sec. Database operations on Passmark score at 7313.73, and Redis SET operations reach 17.18 million operations per second.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the n4-highmem-16 offers a high memory-to-vCPU density suitable for memory-intensive workloads without the overhead of higher vCPU counts. However, the lack of local NVMe storage means all storage operations must rely on network-attached volumes, which may introduce latency tradeoffs. The server is well-suited for memory-bound applications, database operations, text processing, and moderate-scale language model inference tasks.
